_what: barrow_v2 'Fjord Headland' GREYBOX layout, sim frame (Run C-9 Phase 2, lane BX, drax). Built by tools/make_layout_v2.py; proved by tools/validate_layout_v2.py.

_rulings.R-C9-145: layout of record = sketch A (sites/BV3r2-A.png) + sketch B's stream into the mere; spawn plan sites/BV3r2-A_spawns.png; floor WHOLE; straight sea-cave stair, one side open, wide, aligned to centre, top landing flush with p03
_rulings.R-C9-144: Fjord Headland; walkable edge = the land itself per biome; small broken stone ring; larger irregular mere fed by the barrow stream; mini-biomes blending at seams
_rulings.N-C9-BV2-FLOOR-WHOLE: Sim Session option (c): the floor is whole; feel-smaller by art only; a flat/walk-over central feature at (0, 0)
_rulings.N-C9-KP253-ANCHORS: the floor contains all six anchor scatter regions and the open lines to origin

frame.godot_axes: X = x, Y = z (up), Z = y; the camera sits at +Z (south) looking north

camera.law: screen_x = ppm*x ; screen_y = ppm*sin(a)*y - ppm*cos(a)*z ; zero yaw (x screen-right, +y toward camera = screen-down)
camera.godot_camera: Camera3D orthographic, keep_aspect KEEP_HEIGHT, size = viewport_rows / ppm, rotation_degrees = (-pitch, 0, 0), placed at target + D*(0, sin(pitch), cos(pitch)) in Godot axes (X = x, Y = up, Z = y)

provenance.csv_note: the CSV is the level-frame source (sm1/survivalworld_a.map); the pack's sg1 rows are its arena-centred image and are what this layout uses
provenance.scatter_model_basis_verbatim: SIM-ROLLED BOX -- each axis rolled INDEPENDENTLY about the body's own emitter anchor: sx = anchor_x + U(-h, +h), sy = anchor_y + U(-h, +h), with h = placement_extents_m (the half-width, per axis; the magnitude stays in that typed field and is deliberately not repeated here). NOT A DISC: the box's corner sits 1.414 x h from the anchor, so a loader drawing an h-radius circle draws the wrong region and rejects bodies the sim placed correctly.

scatter.⚑ finding: The pack's presentation_defaults.scatter_model says the sim rolls a per-axis BOX of half-width 8 m, NOT an 8 m disc (box corner 11.31 m from the anchor). The brief's 8 m disc is contained in the box. This floor contains every BOX (+1 m), so every body the sim can place is on the floor; it therefore also contains every disc (+1 m) and the brief's ~4,026 m2 disc hull.

floor.rule: WHOLE and convex: the convex hull of the six 8 m scatter BOXES + 1 m (Minkowski sum with a 1 m disc, sampled at 3.75 deg)

min_disc_hull_reference.rule: the brief's minimum: hull of the six 8 m discs + 1 m

edge_by_biome.N: the barrow slope (mound toe, door, standing stones)
edge_by_biome.W: the shore: shingle into shore ice, the wreck
edge_by_biome.S/SSE: the cliff lip (the floor edge IS the lip); the sea cave below, the stair
edge_by_biome.E/SE: the hall yard: hall wall, palisade (pulled back), the fallen gable

land.note: the headland: the floor's southern chain is the cliff lip; land continues N (barrow) and E (hall yard) outside the walkable edge

shore_ice.note: shore ice W and SW of the land, outside the edge

mere.covers: p05's 8 m disc + 0.7 m; reaches the stone circle

stream.note: frozen; rises up the barrow's west flank outside the edge (z follows the land), flush ice where it crosses the floor, ends in the mere

stone_circle.note: small, broken; 6 fallen flat (0.30 m), 2 snapped stumps (0.35 m); the worn path runs through it

zones._how: soft colour zones on the floor; the ground class map (greybox/ground_class_map.png, 4 px/m) is the paint + crater-v5 surface driver. Priority: mere > stream > circle > path (overlay) > the seeded biomes (nearest weighted seed, blended over blend_m at the seams)

grave_ground.reason: the barrow's dead: heather over the graves in front of the King's door

shore_shingle.reason: the beach the wreck drove onto; shingle running into shore ice

cliff_top_rock.reason: wind-scoured headland: thin snow on bare rock and scree above the sea

hall_yard_ash.reason: the burnt hall's yard: trampled ash and soot-black snow

snow_field.reason: open snow binding the biomes (the seams melt into it)

mere_ice.reason: the frozen mere, fed by the barrow stream; p05's dead burst up through it

stream_ice.reason: the frozen stream running down from the barrow into the mere (sketch B)

circle.reason: the broken stone circle at the start: a landmark you walk through

path.reason: the worn path from the King's door through the circle to the cliff stair

stair._ruling: R-C9-145 (Matt): B's straighter stair, one side open to the cliff edge, wide, run aligned toward the centre, top landing flush with the p03 patch; monsters must climb it without getting stuck
stair.axis_points_at: the origin (0, 0): the run is ON the ray origin -> p03, so climbing monsters face the centre

top_landing.north_edge: follows the floor boundary vertex-for-vertex between the two side lines (flush, same z as the floor)

flight.walk_model: a REAL RAMP: one plane under the step nosings, the same slope as the treads' pitch line; the steps are a visual on it. Godot CharacterBody3D floor_max_angle default 45 deg > the slope, so a body walks it without a step-up solver
flight.stair_rule_check: 2R + T = 0.640 m (the comfortable band is 0.60-0.65 m)

bottom_landing.note: the shelf at the sea-cave mouth, just above the water

stair.open_side: EAST: no wall, no rail -- the cliff drop is beside the treads the whole way down
stair.wall_side: WEST: the headland spur's rock face (cliff_spur)
stair.placement: OUTSIDE the floor polygon (it descends the cliff). The sim never reads it; it is the visible delivery path from the cave to the p03 patch.
